text:
mike: quick follow-up from the handoff RFC. hit a weird stale-read during demote+evict in prod yesterday. thought we should triage tradeoffs here.

tara: ugh. how did it happen? handoff race?

mike: short timeline:
- old owner O1 begins demote (epoch 101)
- O1 accepts write W but it's still inflight in memory
- before W durably sequenced, O1 evicts prefix due to slab reclaim and completes demote
- new owner O2 takes epoch 102 and serves a read; the client saw pre-W state -> stale

sasha: that implies our demote path can relinquish ownership while unflushed inflight writes remain reachable only on O1 RAM. not great.

lee: agreed. I see three candidate approaches:
1) conservative: block demote until all inflight writes for that prefix are durably applied (simple but stalls demote)
2) durable-fence: old owner publishes a tiny fence record (digest of pending writes) to control-plane before demote completes; new owner waits for or verifies fence
3) reactive: let demote proceed, but make reads that observe epoch bumps do a quick consistency check (query old owner/sidecar) and retry if needed

tara: (3) is attractive for latency but brittle under crashes/partitions. (2) seems like a good middle ground if fence is fast/durable.

mike: thinking (2) + soft-pin: old owner issues publish_fence(prefix, epoch, digest D) and attempts to persist pending deltas to a local staging log (not full WAL). it also sets a soft-pin to prevent immediate eviction of the in-memory buffers. new owner on seeing epoch bump will: check control-plane for fence(D) within T_handshake; if not seen, call O1 via RPC to reconcile; if O1 unreachable, stall reads for safety (first cut).

sasha: what durability do we need for the fence? control-plane metadata write must be observable by any node that may get the takeover. idempotent and lightweight. if control-plane becomes partitioned, T_handshake needs to be conservative.

lee: ops considerations: if we BLOCK reads when fence missing we introduce availability risk for large prefixes during partitions. perhaps default to blocking for enterprise/high-SLA tenants and offer opt-out for best-effort tenants.

mike: telemetry/observability to add: counters for fence_published, fence_seen_by_new_owner, reconcile_rpc_count, demote_eviction_blocked_count, and histograms for fence_publish_latency and demote_handoff_latency. also emit handoff_trace_id for correlating client traces.

tara: we should also measure memory impact of soft-pin under heavy demotes. last time soft-pinning bumped memory by ~3% in our canary. add a canary flag to gate soft-pin behaviour.

sasha: edge-case: O1 crashes after publishing fence but before flushing staging. new owner sees fence but data not applied anywhere durable. That would be bad unless fence guarantees either staging persisted or system can reconstruct via storage backend. So publish_fence must be coupled with at-least-best-effort flush and a documented crash-fallback.

mike: for crash-fallback options:
- new_owner stalls reads until recovery window expires then triggers read-repair from backend storage (possibly slower)
- or new_owner marks prefix as degraded and returns failures for conflicting reads while emitting an alert
I prefer stall+repair initially. safer and simpler.

lee: tests: add a chaos scenario that forces demote while slab-reclaim and node crash interleave. simulate slow writes, and validate no stale reads under the new handshake. add it to CI as a non-blocking integration test.

tara: action items: 
- mike: prototype demote->publish_fence metadata + soft-pin and add unit tests + chaos scenario (ETA: EOW)
- sasha: write control-plane fence API spec (fields, idempotency, durability SLAs) (ETA: 3d)
- lee: add telemetry and canary flag for soft-pin behavior + dashboard (ETA: 2d)
- tara: update runbook with crash-fallback decision tree and what to do on fence visibility failures (ETA: 1d)

opsbot: created ticket IR-9531: "demote-fence-and-soft-pin-protocol" with suggested test-case demote-crash-slabrace.

mike: thanks. one more design note: keep the fence payload minimal (digest + counts) to avoid big metadata writes and reduce control-plane pressure. we'll iterate on the exact guarantees in Sasha's API doc.

sasha: I'll document three modes for fence durability: soft (metadata only), durable (metadata + staging flush guarantee), and strict (durable + WAL). that'll let tenants choose tradeoffs.

lee: sounds good. blocking-by-default for strict tenants. opt-in for relaxed modes.

tara: :thumbsup:

mike: I'll open PR and link IR-9531. will include canary switches so we can ramp. closing for now, ping me if you want to review the PR.
